title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
authors: Kerem Yurtseven, Shantanu R. Jha, Apoorva Limaye, Risav Pokhrel, Muhammad Waqar Amin
abstract: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.
summary: This paper proposes using an Asymmetrically Threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to create high-fidelity, bias-preserving Controlled-X (CX) gates for Kerr-Cat qubits. By engineering photon-number asymmetry, the authors suppress error propagation from phase-flip to bit-flip errors, achieving high fidelity even in the presence of photon loss. This establishes the ATS coupler as a key component for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates (CX gates) for Kerr-Cat qubits, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: They demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity and show that the proposed ATS coupler significantly improves the noise bias compared to naive implementations.
method: The work relies on numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian and detailed analysis of error propagation under single-photon loss, comparing theoretical derivations with time-domain simulations.
model_or_system: The system uses Kerr-Cat qubits coupled via an Asymmetrically Threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler. The dynamics are analyzed using the full circuit Hamiltonian and the Lindblad master equation to track error rates.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), noise bias ($\eta$), bit-flip error rate ($\Gamma_x$), and phase-flip error rate ($\Gamma_z$).
important_parameters: Gate duration of 50 ns, single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, and the asymmetry parameters of the ATS coupler.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes single-photon loss is the dominant error mechanism and utilizes approximations like the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) and coherent state approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bloch-sphere representation of the logical subspace, the schematic circuit diagram of the resonator-ATS-resonator architecture, and comparisons between theoretical infidelity formulas and direct simulation results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for bias-preserving gates, detailing the ATS coupler mechanism and achieving high fidelity, to analyzing error sources like single-photon loss, and finally characterizing residual nonlinearities and implementing drive corrections.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO/quantum optics as it tackles the practical engineering challenge of building robust quantum gates using superconducting circuit platforms (SQUIDs/Kerr-Cat qubits), requiring deep knowledge of open quantum systems and Hamiltonian engineering.
